blockers.summary: The preprint checklist's OPEN deposit item declares the published archive to be behind the repository by '15 paths changed, 0 added, 0 removed'. At the reviewed commit git says 18 changed, 0 added, 0 removed. The declaration was exactly true one commit earlier and went stale at 05c1cac1 — the very commit the reviewed manifest records as its own git_revision — so the item that authorises the next (irreversible) Zenodo version understates what has moved by three deposited files, two of which it does not mention in any form. This is a defect in the deposit chain, not in the manuscript: no sentence of the paper is made untrue by it, and nothing published is wrong.
blockers.evidence: Re-derived exactly as the repository's own guard does, from the pinned commit's blobs only. deposit-state.json:published.git_revision = 4fd4698daec0c39ac77544083dc35d053a4e1e7e; the archive manifest at the pin records git_revision 05c1cac1e6afd4c0d5fe3bad9823e272728d792d. Comparing the two manifests' {path: sha256} maps: 18 changed, 0 added, 0 removed (n = 18). The checklist at the pin says 15 in two places (heading and body). Walking every commit from 4fd4698d to the pin, the count is 0 through aa55257cf, becomes exactly 15 at 19f9d2b417fd ('round 30: five blockers…') — which is what §3-vii states and enumerates correctly — and becomes 18 at 05c1cac1e6af ('the commit loop: ~9 minutes to 131 s'), which moved three further DEPOSITED files: research/manuscripts/lint_citations.py, research/manuscripts/pinned-figures.json and research/manuscripts/aso/fusion-junction-aso-journal-article-manuscript.docx.build-stamp.json. §3-vii's 'What moved, and why each is a correction rather than churn' list names the two sequence files, both manuscripts, the SI, lit-targets-aso-round7-precedents.json, aso_archive_manifest.py, aso_sequence_manifest.py and 'the four journal PDFs and their build stamps' — the strings 'lint_citations', 'pinned-figures' and 'docx' do not occur anywhere in its 2,655 characters. Its stated cause ('because round 30 improved the paper after it was published') is therefore also incomplete: three of the 18 are not round 30 repairs. Corroborating facts that are NOT in question, all re-derived here: the manifest's git_revision is a real commit on origin/main (aso_archive_manifest.py --check-revision-published exits 0, 'is on a remote-tracking ref'); its clean flag is honest — all 515 inventoried sha256 values equal the blobs at 05c1cac1, 0 missing and 0 mismatched, and --check-archive reports 'manifest inventory is current'; the deposition DOI resolves to the record the repository believes — Actions job 100032854734 read zenodo.org live and printed 'record 22229096 — 10.5281/zenodo.22229096', 'state : done (submitted=True)', 'published : 2026-09-01', 'emc-aso-archive.zip 8808345 bytes md5:957ae067bc96c964', 'PUBLISHED. The DOI both papers cite resolves to this record.', matching deposit-state.json's quoted read-back word for word; and the manifest at 4fd4698d carries archive_content_digest ff4da79f8acf129dc46fffa22cb92fbabbf79bfbb419154dc66b066bc1ca291a, which is the manifest_digest deposit-state.json records for the published version.
blockers.what_edit_would_break_it: Correcting the two numbers alone leaves the defect live, because the count is a function of HEAD: any later commit that touches one of the 515 inventoried paths silently re-stales it, and the guard that should say so does not (see the p1). The silent regression is the reverse one: fixing the p1's guard scope WITHOUT re-measuring, or re-measuring against the working tree rather than against deposit-state.json's published git_revision, would produce a number that is right about the wrong pair. The count must be re-derived from the two manifests at the moment of the deposit decision, and §3-vii's enumeration extended to the files that moved, or the next frozen archive ships under a declaration of what changed that is wrong.

blockers.summary: PUB-ASO's extended report states the seven-base-pair scramble-null rates as those of the dinucleotide-preserving null it names, and prints the MONONUCLEOTIDE arm's values instead. The sentence says "the same null" while its ten-base-pair half correctly reads the dinucleotide ladder and its seven-base-pair half reads a different ensemble, so the two halves cannot both be true. Both printed figures understate, which weakens the safety warning the sentence exists to make. The named journal-article DOCUMENT is clean on this claim; the defect is in the sibling outgoing document that states the same fact.
blockers.evidence: Re-derived from research/modalities/aso-parent-null.json (read-only). scrambled_dinucleotide.cut_ladder['7'] = rate_liable 0.85400 (85.4%), rate_pairing_NR4A3_specifically 0.47871 (47.9%), rate_liable_attributed_to_NR4A3 0.29368 (29.4%). scrambled_mononucleotide.cut_ladder['7'] = rate_liable 0.74266 (74.3%), rate_pairing_NR4A3_specifically 0.38755 (38.8%). The manuscript prints 74.3% and 38.8% -- the mononucleotide values -- for a sentence whose antecedent is the dinucleotide null. The antecedent is explicit and is set in the same bullet: line 1711-1714 reads "on this paper's own null 10.0% of dinucleotide-preserving scrambles pair a parent's whole catalytic gap at the ten-base-pair criterion and 4.0% pair wild-type *NR4A3* specifically", then separates "The mononucleotide arm's corresponding 6.2%" as a different thing. Those ten-base-pair figures re-derive as scrambled_dinucleotide@10 rate_liable 0.09991 (10.0%) and rate_pairing_NR4A3_specifically 0.03968 (4.0%), so repair (2) is correct and reads the dinucleotide ladder. Line 1730-1732 then says "Read at seven, the same null returns 74.3% ... and 38.8%", which is the mononucleotide ladder. Understatement is 85.4-74.3 = 11.1 points on the liability rate and 47.9-38.8 = 9.1 points on the NR4A3-specific rate, in the direction the guard's own docstring calls blocker-worthy: the sentence warns a laboratory that a scramble passing the ten-base-pair rule is NOT certified to spare the parents at a looser cut, and both understatements soften that warning. Corroboration of the mechanism from the round's own correction record, research/manuscripts/aso/fusion-junction-aso-preprint-checklist.md:458-459: "an argmax printed under a membership predicate (23.9% where the words asked for 38.8%)" -- 23.9% is scrambled_mononucleotide@7 rate_liable_attributed_to_NR4A3 (0.23918) and 38.8% is scrambled_mononucleotide@7 rate_pairing_NR4A3_specifically, so the repair moved along the PREDICATE axis inside one ensemble row and never checked the ENSEMBLE axis. The correct membership value for the sentence as written is 47.9%. The neighbouring 38.4% is yet a third quantity (cut_sensitivity.observed_rate_liable_against_NR4A3['7'] = 0.38421, the observed panel's argmax), 0.4 points from the printed figure, so a referee spot-checking this number lands among three near-identical values with different meanings. Everything else in the two documents re-derived clean: the journal article's 87 / 61 / 10.0% / 3.9% / 40.6% / 45.8% / 33.1% / 25.4%, its junction ladder (35, 31, 23, 9, 6 of 38 and 5, 3, 2, 0, 0 of the published five), and the extended report's whole eight-row cut ladder including every Wilson interval, the strongest-null identity at each cut and the four sign changes.
blockers.what_edit_would_break_it: The guard added this round, research/manuscripts/tests/test_the_scramble_null_rates_are_bound_to_their_artifact.py, binds the FIELD and the CUT but not the ENSEMBLE: _rates() unions rate_pairing_NR4A3_specifically across all ten ensembles at the named cut, so any of ten values from 38.8% to 64.4% is admissible at cut seven. It passes on this defect today and will pass on any future substitution of one ensemble for another. Fixing the number alone therefore leaves the class open; the sentence must also name its ensemble, and the guard must bind it. Conversely, if the intended arm really is the mononucleotide one, the words "the same null" are what is false and the fix is in the prose -- but then the ten-base-pair and seven-base-pair halves of one bullet still read two different ensembles under one antecedent.

p1s.summary: test_a_declared_drift_states_the_size_it_actually_has cannot see the blocker above, and is green on a coincidence. It requires the git-derived drift count to appear anywhere in §3's 32,656-character slice, which includes CLOSED items and their retained history. The only standalone '18' in that slice sits inside a '⚠ Superseded, retained (rule 1.2)' quotation in the closed §3-iv, describing a different published record. This is the third recurrence of the defect the test's own docstring documents twice — the first version was satisfied by a '23' inside a git sha, which is why the lookarounds already exclude hex; the scope of the search was never narrowed with them.
p1s.evidence: Simulated the guard's exact logic at the pin (no pytest run): n = 18 from the two manifests; _open_blocking_section slices from '## 3 · Open, and blocking the journal submission' to the next '## ', giving 32,656 characters spanning §3-i through §3-vii; re.search(r'(?<![0-9A-Za-z.])18(?![0-9A-Za-z.])', section) matches exactly once, at the §3-iv text '"**28 differences: 18 changed, 10 added, 0 removed**" (true at `b93499e94`)'. Mutation-tested on a COPY at <scratch>/citations-and-archive-checklist-copy.md (the live tree was never touched; git status shows no manuscript or checklist modification from this seat, and the document digest is unchanged at afd60b9ef7f3…): replacing only that retained-history quotation's '18 changed' with '77 changed' flips the assertion from pass to FAIL while §3-vii's bytes are identical across the mutation and still read '**15 paths changed, 0 added, 0 removed**'. The mutation was asserted to have landed (unique match count 1 before, 'output 28 differences: 18 changed' absent after). So the guard is measuring a retained history quote, not the declaration.
p1s.what_edit_would_break_it: Scoping the search to the open drift item is the fix, but binding it to the literal heading string '### 3-vii' regresses the moment the item is renumbered — the item has already moved through 3-i, 3-iv and 3-vii. Scope it by the property the sibling helper already uses (_open_blocking_section_declares_the_drift finds the item by 'PUBLISHED DEPOSIT IS BEHIND') and search only that item's own slice; and exclude text inside a 'Superseded, retained' marker, which is where every stale count in this file is deliberately kept. Any fix that only tightens the lookarounds again repeats the 2026-08-30 patch and leaves the scope defect untouched.

p1s.summary: Table 1's 'ΔTm floor' column and the Methods sentence behind it convert a computed number into a DIRECTIONAL BOUND on the reagents' fusion-versus-parent selectivity, and the premise that makes it a bound — that adding locked residues to the fusion duplex can only widen the separation — is never stated. Every other adopted premise in this paper is explicitly labelled as adopted; this one, which is the only one that turns a number into a bound in a display item, is not.
p1s.evidence: Manuscript Methods: 'Melting temperatures are nearest-neighbour values for an unmodified DNA:RNA hybrid at 250 nM strand. That is not a locked phosphorothioate oligonucleotide, so no absolute melting point is reported. Only the fusion-versus-parent separation is, and as a floor: the fusion duplex pairs all ten locked residues where each parent pairs five.' The stated justification is a PAIRING COUNT; the inference from that count to a floor requires monotonic, additive LNA stabilisation, which is neither stated nor tested. The producing artifacts label the premise explicitly and the manuscript does not: research/modalities/junction-aso-thermo.json, field '⚠_lna_not_modelled' — 'so LNA widens ΔΔG rather than compressing it, and the discrimination reported here is a conservative FLOOR ... Argued from the architecture, not computed: no LNA parameters are applied.' — and the same file records that this field 'previously said the opposite, that LNA compresses ΔΔG and the value is an UPPER bound', i.e. the direction has already been wrong once here. research/modalities/aso-offtarget-duplex-energy.json, '⚠_lna_not_modelled': 'This premise — more locked pairs, more stabilisation — is the one junction_aso_thermo.py already runs on, and is adopted rather than measured here.' Re-derived: junction-aso-thermo.json per_design gives dtm_discrimination_c 26.6 for GGGCATATCATCAAAC and 36.0 for GGGCATATCTTGTGTG, exactly the '≥ 26.6' and '≥ 36.0' printed in Table 1, so the arithmetic is right and only the word 'floor' is unsupported by anything the reader is shown. Contrast the paper's own handling of every other premise, which is uniformly explicit: 'That premise is adopted here rather than established' (line 86), 'That direction is adopted here rather than retrieved' (line 91), 'ten being adopted rather than measured' (line 123), 'a high-affinity chemistry is taken here to' (line 169), 'that is a premise adopted here rather than a retrieved finding' (line 173), 'Its form and the cut of 5.0 are adopted here as conventions' (line 320).
p1s.what_edit_would_break_it: Nothing binds the word 'floor' to a premise, so two ordinary edits silently remove the bound's justification altogether: (a) renaming Table 1's column from 'ΔTm floor (°C)' to 'ΔTm (°C)' or dropping the '≥', which converts an argued bound into an apparent measurement of a modified oligonucleotide's melting behaviour — the one thing Methods says is not reported; (b) shortening the Methods sentence, whose only tether is the trailing clause 'the fusion duplex pairs all ten locked residues where each parent pairs five'. The table's caption defers to Methods ('The separation is a floor rather than an estimate, for the reason Methods gives'), so an edit to Methods silently strands the caption too. Scoped by property: the ΔTm floor appears in exactly two places in the submitted deliverable — the manuscript Methods sentence and Table 1's column header plus caption — and in no other submission text (grep for 'floor|locked' over the article, SI, tables and cover letter returns no third site).

p1s.summary: The paper's two literature-negative claims — the ones that establish the whole rationale for the work — are made with no search strategy, database, date, query or corpus size anywhere in the deliverable. The evidence exists and is quantified, but only in the deposit and in the companion research article, neither of which this submission carries.
p1s.evidence: Abstract: 'none is reported for any NR4A3 fusion in the literature retrieved.' Introduction: 'No such design is reported for any NR4A3 fusion in the literature retrieved here.' Grep for 'Europe PMC|search|query|retrieved|5153' over the article and the SI returns no search description: Methods opens 'All analyses are computational and use public data' and then goes straight to transcripts and screens. The evidence does exist: research/manuscripts/aso/fusion-junction-aso-priorart-evidence.json records two Europe PMC corpora (aso-priorart-fusiononco n=4252, aso-priorart-junction n=1133, 232 in both, 5153 unique — re-derived: 4252+1133-232=5153, and the file's own counts.agrees_with_manuscript is true), plus the caveat 'a paper indexed under other terms, or not indexed, would not appear'. The COMPANION states it and this deliverable does not: research/manuscripts/aso/fusion-junction-aso-research-article.md:139 reads 'across 5,153 unique records retrieved from Europe PMC'. That this is genuinely absent from what a referee receives is fixed by the build record: research/manuscripts/aso/fusion-junction-aso-journal-article.build-stamp.json lists built_from as the article, the journal references, the journal tables, the sequence CSV and one figure SVG — the SI is not part of this deliverable, and the SI's own front matter says its numbered cross-references point at 'fusion-junction-aso-research-article.md', a document this referee would not hold.
p1s.what_edit_would_break_it: The entire bound is carried by one participle. Deleting 'retrieved' from either sentence — the obvious copy-edit, since 'in the literature retrieved' reads as clumsy to a copy editor — turns a bounded search result into an absolute priority claim, and because the article contains no search description at all, nothing else in the document would then contradict it. The same regression is available by moving the claim into a shorter abstract. Scoped by property: the claim has exactly two sites in this deliverable (line 45 and line 80) and both are worded identically, so a fix applied to one and not the other leaves the abstract — the part a referee reads first — unbounded.

p1s.summary: Every 'clean' and 'no near-match' statement in the paper rests on a heuristic aligner with a computable blind spot that the paper never states: at blastn-short's word size of 7, one eighth of two-mismatch configurations of a 16-mer cannot be seeded at all. The one bound the paper does give for clean counts runs in the opposite direction, so a reader is told the count is conservative when the unstated limitation makes it anti-conservative.
p1s.evidence: The alignment arm is 'blastn (short, FILTER off)' against refseq_rna at '>= 14/16 identical' (research/modalities/junction-aso-offtarget-e12n3-deep500-b1.json, method.program and method.near_match_threshold). I re-derived the blind spot from scratch rather than from any prose: over C(16,2)=120 two-mismatch configurations, the two mismatches cut the 16-mer into at most three exactly-matched runs; 15 of the 120 leave no run of 7 or more and therefore cannot be seeded at a word size of 7 — 12.5% of the class, unreachable at any search depth. So 'Three designs clear every screen at the ten-base-pair criterion' is a property of this search, not of the transcriptome, and the same applies to 'The TAF15 reagent carries no sense-strand precursor site' as far as the alignment arm is concerned (that particular statement is separately safe, because the precursor arm is exhaustive by construction — aso-premrna-offtarget.json method.completeness). The paper states the wrong-signed bound instead: 'a count of clean designs is a floor over that subset, not a total over the panel' — a floor means the true clean count could be higher, whereas an unseeded near-match means a design called CLEAN may not be. The companion carries the correct bound and this deliverable drops it: research/manuscripts/aso/fusion-junction-aso-research-article.md:1996-2003, 'BLAST's sensitivity at >=14/16 is bounded rather than unquantified ... 15 of the 120 two-mismatch configurations leave no exact seven-mer and cannot be seeded at all — about an eighth of the class, unreachable at any depth. So "no sense-strand near-match" is a property of this search and not of the transcriptome.' Grep for 'sensitiv|heuristic|BLAST|word size|E-value' over the journal article returns nothing but the word 'RefSeq' at line 112.
p1s.what_edit_would_break_it: This is already the regressed state rather than a risk: the bound exists, is quantified, and is present in the sibling document at the same pin, and it was lost in the cut to the journal length. The silent-regression risk going forward is that any repair added to the journal article will have a sibling in the research article whose numbers must move together — the pair 'about an eighth' / '15 of the 120' appears in exactly one of the two documents today, so a future re-measurement (a different word size, a different identity threshold) would update one site and leave the other stale, which is the one-of-a-pair defect this corpus has produced before. Note also that the paper's stated 14-of-16 threshold is what makes the arithmetic computable: raising or lowering it changes 15/120 and would need both sites re-derived.

p1s.summary: The paragraph that bounds every clean count gives DEFAULT-depth denominators, while the only clean count the paper prints is a DEEP-depth result. The bound as scoped does not describe the subset the count is taken over, and it understates how complete that subset actually is.
p1s.evidence: The article: 'Two bounds apply to any count of designs called CLEAN by the alignment screen, and to those only ... First, seven of the 190 alignment screens never returned, and that screen censors the rest, leaving 47 of 183 assessable for cleanliness.' Recounted directly over the committed screens at this pin. DEFAULT depth (the 38 junction-aso-offtarget-<j>.json files, 16-mers only): 190 design slots, 7 with status 'screen_failed' (three at EWSR1 e9, one each at FUS e3, TAF15 e12, TCF12 e7, TCF12 e9), 183 screened, and 47 of those 183 have n_offtarget_near_matches <= 15, i.e. a stored hit list that is not right-censored — exactly the paper's four numerals. DEEP depth (the -deep500 / -clean9-deep500 files): 187 screened, 3 failed. The printed clean count comes from the deep arm: research/modalities/aso-per-junction-table.json is built with select=ass.is_deep (research/modalities/aso_per_junction_table.py:235), sums to 187 n_designs_screened and 3 n_designs_absent_because_the_deep_screen_did_not_return, and the three designs I recovered from it by requiring parent_is_liability false, n_hybridisable 0 and premrna_gap_paired_hybridisable 0 are AGGGCATATCGGAGTC (FUS e8), GGGCATATCCGACATG (TAF15 e1) and GGGCATATCAAGCGCT (TCF12 e7) — exactly three, two with a longest parent duplex of 0 and one at 8 bp against wild-type NR4A3, and none at a junction tiered 'published_exon_resolved_breakpoint', which is what the sentence claims. The paper already names the depth for a different number three paragraphs earlier ('at a deeper search ceiling than the default'), so the reader can see two depths are in play and cannot tell which the bound belongs to.
p1s.what_edit_would_break_it: The two halves live in different paragraphs with no textual link, so a future re-run at one depth updates one and not the other. Concretely: if the default-depth screens are ever re-run and the seven failures resolve, '7 of 190' and '47 of 183' move while 'Three designs clear every screen' does not — and vice versa. Naming the depth inside the bounding sentence, as the article already does at line 156, is what would make the pair fail together instead of drifting apart. Scoped by property: I checked every other numeral in the article that could carry a depth and only these two families do — the parent, precursor, genome-wide and duplex-energy counts run over all 190 with no failures and no censoring, which the same paragraph correctly says.

p1s.summary: The new scramble-null guard cannot see the ensemble axis, so it certifies the blocker above and would certify any ensemble substitution. It is the guard this round added to stop exactly this class of error, and it passes while the defect is present.
p1s.evidence: Replicated the guard's logic read-only (no pytest run against this repository) and mutation-tested it on scratch COPIES of the documents at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Rare-cancers/d7df5340-da31-515e-943e-cf65c62ed12d/scratchpad/round31/out/regression-mut/, never the live tree; `git status --porcelain` over research/manuscripts/ is unchanged and the two documents still hash to afd60b9e... and 2b495c48... . Each mutation was confirmed to land (search-string count before and after) before its result was read. Substituting the cut-seven figure 38.8% -> 47.9% (scrambled_dinucleotide@7, the correct value) PASSES; -> 64.0% (exon_terminus_chimera@7) PASSES; -> 52.3% (random_parent_chimera@7) PASSES; -> 5.7% (a value no ensemble carries at cut seven) FAILS. So the guard discriminates only "is this number in the membership field somewhere at this cut", which is true of ten different ensembles. The guard's own docstring states the round-30 blocker it exists to prevent recurring and its positive control test_the_two_readings_really_do_differ_so_this_guard_is_not_vacuous asserts only that the argmax and membership fields differ at scrambled_mononucleotide@7; nothing asserts that the ensemble a sentence names is the ensemble whose row is printed. The cut-binding the guard does carry is real and works -- the documented mutation 4.0% -> 3.9% at cut ten is caught, because 3.9 belongs to no membership row at cut ten (allowed there: 1.9, 2.0, 2.2, 3.3, 3.6, 4.0, 8.9, 9.8, 28.9, 29.3) even though it is a legitimate membership value at exon_terminus_chimera_novel_acceptor@13.
p1s.what_edit_would_break_it: Any repair that changes the printed number without adding an ensemble term to both the prose and the guard leaves the guard green and the class open. Adding an ensemble term to the guard requires the prose to name its arm; a guard that infers the arm from nearby words would re-introduce the punctuation-fragility the manifest module documents at its own `quote` probe.

p1s.summary: The extended report's cut-ladder table has a column headed only "scramble null %" while the paper defines two scramble ensembles that differ by up to 14 points at the cuts it tabulates. The column carries the mononucleotide arm; the scramble a laboratory is actually asked to draw is the dinucleotide one. This is the ambiguity the blocker above fell into.
p1s.evidence: Every value in the column re-derives as scrambled_mononucleotide.cut_ladder rate_liable: 91.4, 74.3, 43.8, 18.4, 6.2, 1.8, 0.4, 0.1 at cuts 6-13 (artifact: 0.91437, 0.74266, 0.43753, 0.18390, 0.06179, 0.01824, 0.00404, 0.00074). The dinucleotide arm at the same cuts is 96.7, 85.4, 57.3, 27.2, 10.0, 3.5, 0.8, 0.2. Section 4.4 specifies the control to be made as "a dinucleotide-preserving shuffle -- the control 4.4 asks a laboratory to make" (line 708-709), so the table's unlabelled column is not the null that governs the control. By contrast the adjacent "strongest null %" column does name its ensemble in every cell ("exon-terminus", "exon-terminus, novel acceptor"), and that naming re-derives correctly at every cut, which is the pattern this column does not follow.
p1s.what_edit_would_break_it: Relabelling the column without re-checking every downstream sentence that quotes a value from it: the 74.3% in 4.4 was read out of this column and attributed to the other arm. Any future cut added to the ladder inherits the same unlabelled column.

p1s.summary: The '95% interval' that carries the paper's only inferential comparison against the nulls is a Wilson binomial interval computed as if the 190 designs were independent Bernoulli draws — an assumption the producing artifact itself states the data violate — and the manuscript names neither the construction, the sidedness, nor the assumption.
p1s.evidence: The sentence is 'at ten the strongest null's 40.6% falls inside the panel's own 95% interval on 45.8%, as at every cut from seven to thirteen but eleven.' I re-derived both halves exactly from research/modalities/aso-parent-null.json: the interval is `cut_sensitivity.observed_cut_ladder['10'].rate_liable_wilson95` = [0.38859, 0.52887] on 87/190 = 0.45789, and the strongest null at cut 10 is `null_ensembles.exon_terminus_chimera.rate_liable` = 0.40568, inside it. Walking cuts 6-13 with each cut's own panel Wilson interval and a per-cut argmax over the ten ensembles, the null falls inside at 7,8,9,10,12,13 and outside at 6 and 11 — so 'every cut from seven to thirteen but eleven' is exact. The construction, however, is only in the artifact, and that same artifact's `_what_this_is_not[0]` says: 'Not a significance test. The 190 design records are 176 distinct molecules tiled at overlapping registers across 38 junctions, so they are not independent draws and no test treating them as such would be right about its own denominator. Proportions carry Wilson intervals; the per-design paired rate is the honest comparison.' The manuscript uses the interval as exactly the test the artifact disclaims, and carries none of that sentence. Nothing in the manuscript or the SI contains the word 'Wilson' (grep over fusion-junction-aso-journal-article.md and fusion-junction-aso-supplementary-information.md: 'Wilson' appears only in the SI's coverage-ladder paragraph, line 147, about a different quantity). The one place the article does state sidedness is the Discussion's 'two-sided 95% interval' (line 326), so the Results sentence is also inconsistent with the paper's own standard one section later. I checked the direction and the claim survives: designs cluster 5-per-junction, ANOVA ICC at cut 10 is 0.106 (design effect 1.42) and at cut 11 is 0.057 (deff 1.23), so a deff-adjusted Wilson interval at cut 11 is [0.36625, 0.52076] and a 4000-replicate junction-level cluster bootstrap gives [0.36316, 0.52105] — the null's 0.34679 is outside all three, so the 'but eleven' exception is not an artifact of the independence assumption. De-duplicating to the 176 distinct sequences (taking each sequence's longest run) leaves the inside/outside pattern identical at all eight cuts. Sign changes of (panel - strongest null) across cuts 6-13 is 4, matching 'changes sign four times', and it is 4 against either exon-terminus ensemble held fixed as well.
p1s.what_edit_would_break_it: The interval's construction lives only in the artifact, so nothing in the manuscript's guard set pins it. research/manuscripts/tests/test_journal_article_numbers.py binds the 45.8%/40.6% figures and the 'seven to thirteen but eleven' string to the artifact's numbers, but no guard binds the prose to a stated interval TYPE or to a stated independence assumption, because the prose states neither. If aso_parent_null.py's denominator is ever changed to the 176 distinct sequences, or the ensembles are re-drawn at a different `draws_per_design_per_ensemble` (currently 200), the interval moves and the sentence re-derives against whatever the artifact then holds — a reader can never tell which population the interval was over, and 'the panel's own 95% interval' reads identically either way. The same sentence would also survive unchanged if a future edit reported a per-junction or cluster-robust interval instead, which is the honest comparison the artifact names.

p1s.summary: The pre-registered replicate standard deviation of 0.35 never names the quantity it is the standard deviation OF, and the two available readings differ by a factor of sqrt(2) — enough to move the headline power at six replicates from about 80% to about 50%, which is the number that sets the prescribed replicate count.
p1s.evidence: Line 322-324 reads 'At an assumed replicate standard deviation of 0.35 on the natural-log scale ... six independent biological replicates give about 80% power to falsify a true selectivity of 3 and three give about 30%.' Selectivity was defined one sentence earlier as a RATIO of two IC50s, so 0.35 could be the replicate SD of the log RATIO or the replicate SD of a single arm's log IC50. Running the producing module (research/manuscripts/aso_falsification_power.py, copied to scratch and run read-only) reproduces the printed figures exactly under the first reading: power 30.42% at n=3, 81.28% at n=6, 98.31% at n=10; void SDs 0.648, 1.534, 2.250 — so 'about 30%', 'about 80%', 'about 0.65', '1.53', '2.25' are all correct as printed, and the noncentral-t construction (t_crit = t.ppf(0.025, n-1), ncp = (ln3 - ln5)*sqrt(n)/sigma) is the right one for 'the upper limit of a two-sided 95% interval below 5'. Under the second reading with independent arms, sigma_ratio = 0.35*sqrt(2) = 0.495 and the same module gives 18.65% at n=3, 53.13% at n=6, 82.68% at n=10 — 'about 80% at six' becomes 'about 50% at six', and six replicates would no longer be the count a reader would pre-register. The paper's 'from a matched dose-response in the same wells' makes the arms paired, which puts the true ratio SD somewhere in [0, 0.495] but does not tell the reader which end 0.35 names. The module's own docstring is equally silent ('the underlying replicate SD of 0.35 on the natural-log scale'), so the referent exists nowhere in the repository. The void-SD figures are unambiguous by construction — they are SDs of the log ratio, since they are derived from the interval itself, log(5)*sqrt(n)/t_{.975,n-1} — which means the paper uses one unnamed symbol in two roles that must be the same quantity and never says so.
p1s.what_edit_would_break_it: research/manuscripts/tests/test_journal_article_numbers.py::test_the_falsification_power_figures_are_derived_not_typed binds the five printed figures to aso_falsification_power.power_pct/void_sd, but its two regexes ('six independent biological replicates give about (\d+)% power ...' and 'about (\d+\.\d+) at three replicates ...') do not capture the '0.35' at all, and grep for 'SIGMA' or 'replicate standard deviation' across research/manuscripts/tests and research/modalities/tests returns no binding of the article's literal 0.35 to the module's SIGMA. So the prose figure 0.35 can be edited to any other number, or the phrase can be shortened past its 'on the natural-log scale' qualifier, and every gate stays green while the stated assumption and the computed power silently stop describing each other.
